audience.text: Python developers building tools that parse, inspect, modify, and serialize HTML documents with WHATWG DOM and CSSOM APIs.

capabilities.text: Parse HTML strings, fragments, and files into a DOM document using HTMLDocument.parse, parse_fragment, and load methods.
capabilities.title: Parse HTML into DOM

capabilities.text: Create, append, and modify DOM nodes using Document.create_element, Element methods, and attribute/dataset/text_content accessors.
capabilities.title: DOM manipulation

capabilities.text: Attach CSS stylesheets, match selectors, and resolve computed styles using CSSStyleSheet and ComputedStyleDeclaration.
capabilities.title: CSSOM styling

capabilities.text: Parse, normalize, and manipulate URLs and query strings using URL and URLSearchParams classes.
capabilities.title: URL handling

capabilities.text: Detect character encodings from byte streams using detect_encoding, supporting BOM, meta-charset, and UTF-8 defaults.
capabilities.title: Encoding detection

capabilities.text: Execute JavaScript against a parsed DOM using JSContext backed by QuickJS, with module registration support.
capabilities.title: JavaScript execution

capabilities.text: Serialize documents, fragments, or elements to HTML strings using serialise, outer_html, and inner_html.
capabilities.title: Serialization

capabilities.text: Drive the WHATWG-compliant tokenizer directly to inspect token types and states for custom parsing workflows.
capabilities.title: Tokenizer control

limitations.text: CSS selector matching omits several dynamic and legacy pseudo-classes, raising NotImplementedError in the matcher and parser.
CSSRule.type and CSSRule.css_text are not implemented; concrete rule subclasses expose their own properties instead.
Form constraint validation (validity-state computation) and HTMLImageElement.decode() are present on the API surface but not yet implemented.
The library builds internal layout structures but does not expose a public API for rendering documents to an image or PDF.
JavaScript execution via JSContext requires the optional quickjs extra and exposes a read-only DOM proxy; dynamic import() is not implemented.
Single-colon legacy pseudo-element forms are not parsed by the CSS selector parser.

problems_solved.text: Parsing HTML strings, fragments, and files into a standards-compliant DOM tree using WHATWG tokenization and tree-construction algorithms.
Resolving computed styles and matching CSS selectors against DOM elements using a CSSOM-based cascade implementation.
Validating and manipulating URLs and query strings with WHATWG-compliant URL and URLSearchParams APIs.
Detecting character encodings from byte streams using BOM and content sniffing.

product_summary.text: Aspose.HTML FOSS for Python is an open-source Python library for parsing HTML into a standards-based DOM tree, applying CSS, serializing markup, and optionally executing JavaScript via QuickJS.

uncertainties: The exact set of unimplemented pseudo-classes beyond those explicitly mentioned is not fully listed in the facts.
The behavior of HTMLDocument.load for non-file inputs is not demonstrated in examples or clarified in symbols.
Whether the layout module supports any rendering output beyond internal structures is not confirmed by public symbols.
The scope of JSContext's DOM proxy (e.g., write-only properties, mutation behavior) is not detailed beyond evaluate.
The handling of relative vs absolute URLs in URL.parse when no base is provided is not explicitly shown.
The behavior of detect_encoding when multiple conflicting encodings are detected is not detailed.
The threading model or reentrancy guarantees of JSContext are not specified in the available facts.
The versioning and compatibility guarantees for the 243 public types are not stated in the facts.

workflows.name: Parse and mutate HTML
workflows.text: Parse an HTML string into an HTMLDocument, create and append new elements, and serialize the updated fragment using serialise().

workflows.name: Apply and inspect CSS
workflows.text: Attach a CSSStyleSheet to a Document, set element attributes, and resolve computed styles using get_computed_style().

workflows.name: Query DOM elements
workflows.text: Select elements by tag name, ID, or class using get_element_by_id, get_elements_by_tag_name, and TreeWalker/NodeIterator.

workflows.name: Execute JavaScript
workflows.text: Create a JSContext bound to a Document and evaluate JavaScript expressions against the DOM using evaluate().

workflows.name: Tokenize HTML directly
workflows.text: Instantiate a Tokenizer with raw HTML text and iterate over tokens to inspect tag names and states.

workflows.name: Handle URLs and query parameters
workflows.text: Parse a URL, modify its search parameters, and serialize the updated URL string.
